Title: Lawfulness, fairness and transparency
Description: Personal data must be processed lawfully fairly and in a transparent manner in relation to the data subject.

Title: Purpose limitation
Description: Personal data must be collected for specified explicit and legitimate purposes and not further processed in a manner incompatible with those purposes.

Title: Data minimization
Description: Personal data must be adequate relevant and limited to what is necessary in relation to the purposes for which it is processed.

Title: Accuracy
Description: Personal data must be accurate and where necessary kept up to date; inaccurate data must be erased or rectified without delay.

Title: Storage limitation
Description: Personal data must be kept in a form permitting identification of data subjects for no longer than is necessary for the purposes for which it is processed.

Title: Integrity and confidentiality
Description: Personal data must be processed with appropriate security, including protection against unauthorized or unlawful processing and against accidental loss destruction or damage.

Title: Accountability
Description: The controller is responsible for and must be able to demonstrate compliance with the principles set out in Article 5(1).

Title: Consent
Description: The data subject has given consent to the processing of their personal data for one or more specific purposes.

Title: Contract
Description: Processing is necessary for the performance of a contract with the data subject or to take steps prior to entering into a contract.

Title: Legal obligation
Description: Processing is necessary for compliance with a legal obligation to which the controller is subject.

Title: Vital interests
Description: Processing is necessary to protect the vital interests of the data subject or of another natural person.

Title: Public task
Description: Processing is necessary for the performance of a task carried out in the public interest or in the exercise of official authority vested in the controller.

Title: Legitimate interests
Description: Processing is necessary for the legitimate interests of the controller or a third party, except where overridden by the interests or fundamental rights of the data subject.

Title: Conditions for valid consent
Description: The controller must be able to demonstrate that consent was given, and requests for consent must be presented in a clear and plain manner distinguishable from other matters.

Title: Right to withdraw consent
Description: The data subject has the right to withdraw consent at any time and it must be as easy to withdraw consent as it was to give it.

Title: Conditions applicable to a child's consent
Description: Sets the age, as low as 13 and defaulting to 16, below which parental or guardian consent is required for information society services offered directly to a child.

Title: Prohibition on processing special categories of data
Description: Processing of data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, trade union membership, and the processing of genetic, biometric, or health data or data concerning a person's sex life or sexual orientation, is prohibited by default.

Title: Conditions lifting the prohibition
Description: Lists the exceptions permitting special category processing such as explicit consent; employment and social security law; vital interests; legal claims; and substantial public interest.

Title: Processing of criminal conviction and offence data
Description: Processing of personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences is only permitted under the control of an official authority or when authorized by law with appropriate safeguards.

Title: Transparent information and communication
Description: The controller must provide information and communications to data subjects in a concise transparent intelligible and easily accessible form using clear and plain language.

Title: Information to be provided (data collected from the subject)
Description: Specifies the information a controller must give a data subject at the time personal data is collected directly from them.

Title: Information to be provided (data not obtained from the subject)
Description: Specifies the information a controller must give when personal data has been obtained from a source other than the data subject.

Title: Right of access
Description: The data subject has the right to obtain confirmation of and access to their personal data along with specified supplementary information.

Title: Right to rectification
Description: The data subject has the right to have inaccurate personal data corrected and incomplete personal data completed.

Title: Right to erasure ('right to be forgotten')
Description: The data subject has the right to obtain erasure of personal data without undue delay where one of the specified grounds applies.

Title: Right to restriction of processing
Description: The data subject has the right to obtain restriction of processing under specified circumstances such as contested accuracy.

Title: Notification obligation regarding rectification erasure or restriction
Description: The controller must communicate any rectification, erasure, or restriction to each recipient the data was disclosed to, unless this proves impossible or involves disproportionate effort.

Title: Right to data portability
Description: The data subject has the right to receive their personal data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format and to transmit it to another controller.

Title: Right to object
Description: The data subject has the right to object at any time to processing based on legitimate interests or public task grounds or to processing for direct marketing purposes.

Title: Automated individual decision-making, including profiling
Description: The data subject has the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal or similarly significant effects.

Title: Responsibility of the controller
Description: The controller must implement appropriate technical and organizational measures to ensure and be able to demonstrate that processing complies with the Regulation.

Title: Data protection by design and by default
Description: The controller must implement measures designed to give effect to data protection principles and by default limit processing to what is necessary for each specific purpose.

Title: Joint controllers
Description: Where two or more controllers jointly determine the purposes and means of processing they must transparently determine their respective responsibilities.

Title: Representatives not established in the Union
Description: Controllers or processors not established in the Union but subject to it under Article 3(2) must designate, in writing, a representative in the Union.

Title: Processor obligations and data processing agreements
Description: Processing carried out by a processor must be governed by a binding contract or data processing agreement setting out the subject matter duration nature and purpose of processing and the obligations and rights of the parties.

Title: Processing under the authority of the controller or processor
Description: Any person acting under the authority of the controller or processor who has access to personal data may only process it on instructions from the controller unless required to do so by law.

Title: Records of processing activities (RoPA)
Description: Controllers and processors must maintain a written record of the processing activities carried out under their responsibility.

Title: Security of processing
Description: Implement appropriate technical and organizational measures, such as pseudonymization, encryption, and resilience testing, to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk.

Title: Notification to the supervisory authority
Description: The controller must notify a personal data breach to the competent supervisory authority without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of becoming aware of it.

Title: Communication to the data subject
Description: The controller must communicate a personal data breach to affected data subjects without undue delay when the breach is likely to result in a high risk to their rights and freedoms.

Title: DPIA requirement
Description: The controller must carry out a data protection impact assessment prior to processing that is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons.

Title: Prior consultation
Description: The controller must consult the supervisory authority prior to processing when a DPIA indicates a high residual risk in the absence of mitigating measures.

Title: Designation of the DPO
Description: A controller or processor must designate a DPO where required, such as for a public authority, large-scale systematic monitoring, or large-scale processing of special category data.

Title: Position of the DPO
Description: The DPO must be involved properly and in a timely manner in all data protection matters, be given adequate resources, report to the highest management level, and must not be dismissed or penalized for performing their duties.

Title: Tasks of the DPO
Description: DPO tasks include informing and advising on obligations, monitoring compliance, advising on DPIAs, and cooperating with and acting as the contact point for the supervisory authority.

Title: General principle for transfers
Description: Any transfer of personal data to a third country or international organization must comply with the conditions set out in Chapter V of the Regulation.

Title: Adequacy decisions
Description: Transfers may be made to a third country territory or sector that the European Commission has decided ensures an adequate level of data protection without needing further authorization.

Title: Appropriate safeguards (e.g. Standard Contractual Clauses)
Description: Absent an adequacy decision, a transfer may proceed if the controller or processor has provided appropriate safeguards, such as Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs).

Title: Binding Corporate Rules (BCRs)
Description: Approved Binding Corporate Rules allow intra-group transfers within a multinational organization subject to approval by a competent supervisory authority.

Title: Derogations for specific situations
Description: Absent adequacy or appropriate safeguards, transfers may occur under specific derogations such as explicit consent, contract necessity, or important public interest reasons, as a last resort.
